title: Serving Runtime Leadership Pulseboard - May 11 2027
content:
Meeting: Serving Runtime — Cross-Team Leadership Pulseboard
Date: 2027-05-11
Time: 09:30–10:15 PT (45m)
Attendees: Aisha (chair), Mateo, Jin, Lena, Samir, Priya, reps from SRE and Platform-Eng (joined at 9:50)

Purpose and framing:
- Quick, operationally-focused sync to surface sprint risks, customer-impacting regressions, and decisions that need cross-team alignment. Keep actions tight; escalate blockers to execs only when we don’t have an owner.

1) Sprint health (30s tiles by subteam)
- Runtime Core: build green 98% after kernel fix; smoke tests flaky on long-context (>=8k) sequences; velocity 80% of commitment due to extra investigation time.
- Compiler & Kernels: merged fallback kernel for causal attention (PR 782); still optimizing memory bandwidth for quantized paths.
- Orchestration: canary rollout for kv-cache split enabled for 15% of traffic in region us-west1; autoscaler edge-case seen with burst traffic.
- SRE: increased alert rate for p95 token latency on dedicated clusters; two customer incidents (CUST-441, CUST-443) opened overnight.
- Private Deployments: preparing 2.2.0 customer build with backport of kernel-fallback; ETA 5/14 for first on-prem demo.
- Optimize team: batch size recommendation engine prototype running; initial tests show 12–18% token-cost savings for chat workloads.

2) Major incidents / regressions (10m)
- Latency spike summary: starting 2027-05-10 02:00 UTC, p95 token latency increased by ~40% on A100-backed nodes for sequences >8k tokens.
  - Root cause (working hypothesis): a kernel selection regression caused the runtime to choose a non-vectorized path for long sequences when a new compiler flag is set.
  - Impact: 2 dedicated customers hit SLA alerts, several hosted tenants saw degraded tail latency but no data loss.
  - Mitigation in progress: reverted flag in staging; deployed kernel-fallback to canary in prod (JIRA INF-3421).
  - Next steps: profiler run across failing traces (owner: Jin, due: 2027-05-12), follow-up postmortem if root cause confirmed.

3) Canary/KPIs and rollout decisions (5m)
- kv-cache split rollout: currently at 15% us-west1. Observed ~8% drop in median latency for read-heavy workloads.
  - Decision: expand to 40% tomorrow 05/12 morning contingent on no error-rate increase >0.5%. Owner: Mateo.
- Kernel-fallback: keep enabled globally until profiler validates fix; revert plan prepared if any correctness regressions seen. Owner: Jin.

4) Cross-team blockers and asks (7m)
- Orchestration -> Runtime: need a small API tweak (stateless probe) to allow pods to signal warm-cache readiness before accepting traffic. Impact: reduces cold-start latency for burst workloads. Owner: Samir; requested design doc link in Confluence by 05/13.
- SRE -> Compiler: a monitoring metric for memory bandwidth per-GPU is missing; SRE needs this to correlate slowdowns. Owner: Lena; action: add telemetry in next sprint.
- Private Deployments -> Security: customers requested attestable kernel version list for compliance. Owner: Priya to coordinate with security and PM.

5) Customer & Sales notes (2m)
- Dedicated customer ACME Foods (CUST-441) affected by latency spike; SRE and Solutions Eng to lead remediation comms. 1:1 scheduled 05/11 14:00 PT.
- Sales ask: a short one-pager on impact/rollback story for canaries to share with prospects. Owner: Mateo; deliverable 05/13.

6) Decisions and trade-offs captured
- Keep kernel-fallback enabled globally as safety net (trade-off: slightly higher median cost vs. lower risk of regression).
- Expand kv-cache split cautiously to 40% to capture latency gains; rollback threshold set at error-rate delta >0.5%.

7) Action items (owners + due dates)
- Jin: Complete profiler traces and narrow root cause of long-context kernel selection (due 2027-05-12).
- Mateo: Expand kv-cache canary to 40% and monitor error-rate; post rollout report (due 2027-05-12 EOD).
- Samir: Draft stateless-ready probe API design and post to Confluence (due 2027-05-13).
- Lena: Add per-GPU memory-bandwidth metric to telemetry and run correlation dashboard (due 2027-05-18).
- Priya: Compile attested kernel-version list for private customers and coordinate with Security (due 2027-05-14).
- Aisha: Write short incident note and coordinate follow-up postmortem (due 2027-05-13).

8) Risks flagged (one-line)
- Longer-term: if kernel-selection heuristics continue to diverge across quantized paths we risk repeated regressions on long-context workloads.
- Capacity: autoscaler edge-case during burst traffic could cause transient unavailability for high-throughput customers.

9) Parking lot / topics for next meeting
- Quick sync on quantization compatibility matrix and test coverage (request: compiler + QA).
- Explore automated rollback orchestration for canary expansions.

Meeting notes author: Aisha Patel
Next meeting: 2027-05-18 09:30 PT
